ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The square $ABCD$ consists of four congruent rectangles arranged around a central square. The perimeter of each of the rectangles is $40\mathrm{~cm}$. What is the area of the square $ABCD$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows an outer square labeled ABCD, with A at the bottom-left, B at the bottom-right, C at the top-right, and D at the top-left. Inside the square are four congruent gray rectangles arranged around a central white square: one along the top, one along the right side, one along the bottom, and one along the left side. Reasoning: Let the side lengths of each gray rectangle be l and w. From the arrangement in the image, each side of the large square ABCD is made of one long side of a rectangle plus one short side of a congruent rectangle, so the side length of square ABCD is l + w. Each rectangle has perimeter 40 cm, so 2(l + w) = 40. Therefore l + w = 20, meaning the side length of square ABCD is 20 cm. Its area is 20^2 = 400 square centimeters.
